title: tests(mobile): E2E for the nonce & approval draft editors
description:
## What it solves

Adds Maestro coverage for the two draft-transaction editors on the confirm screen (nonce editor, approval editor), which had none.

## How this PR fixes it

New `transactions/draft-editors/` suite:

- **send-nonce-editor** — drives the real send flow to a draft, edits the nonce (too-low validation, custom rebuild, recommended re-pick), and verifies the transaction details show the same nonce after each change.
- **approval-editor** — composes an approve multiSend draft (the editors only render for drafts), edits the amount and toggles unlimited, and verifies the approve action's on-chain `_value` and spender after each change.

Harness: a `draftEditorsSetup` that seeds the send flow / composes the draft and surfaces its async outcome as `e2e-draft-setup-*` markers. Two small product tweaks make elements addressable: `accessible={false}` on `DialogModal` (also fixes a real VoiceOver grouping bug) and a `testID` on the review-and-confirm button.

## How to test it

```bash
yarn workspace @safe-global/mobile e2e:metro-ios
maestro test --include-tags draft-editors apps/mobile/e2e
```

## Affected flows

- None in production — e2e-only, plus `accessible={false}` on `DialogModal` and one `testID`.

## Blast radius

- `DialogModal` (used by `CustomNonceModal`, `AddToAddressBookModal`) and `ReviewFooter` — additive, no behavior change.
- Flows read live Sepolia staging (Safe data, COW balance); nothing is signed or proposed.

## Risks / not checked

- Approval flow depends on the test Safe holding COW on staging (token symbol/metadata).

## Visual summary

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[compose / send-flow draft] --> B[confirm screen editor]
    B --> C[edit nonce / approval]
    C --> D[draft rebuilds under new safeTxHash]
    D --> E[assert row + tx details / action value]
```

## Checklist

- [x] I've tested the branch on mobile 📱
- [x] I've documented how it affects the analytics (if at all) 📊
- [x] I've written a unit/e2e test for it (if applicable) 🧑‍💻
- [x] I've listed affected flows and blast radius, and named what I did not verify 🎯

---

With the submission of this Pull Request, I confirm that I have read and agree to the terms of the [Contributor License Agreement](https://safe.global/cla).

findings.claim: There is no test covering the waitFor timeout path for setupApprovalDraft's 'chain config' and 'Safe SDK' waits, which are the most likely places to surface real E2E flakiness from SDK initialization timing; a test simulating undefined returns to verify the failure marker/throw would catch regressions there.

E2E_OWNER_ADDRESS duplicates a value that is already available as mockedActiveSafeInfo.owners[0].value, whereas connectSignerSetup.ts derives the same address from that source instead of hardcoding it.

The test mocks the CGW call directly rather than using MSW, which the root AGENTS.md instructs for network calls and which 19 other test files follow, though some existing tests mock initiate().unwrap() similarly for RTK Query code, so it is unclear whether this deviation is acceptable.
The spender address inside APPROVE_DATA is also a hardcoded literal duplicating owners[1] from the shared mock data rather than referencing it directly.

Two sequential waitFor calls in the setup can each take up to 20 seconds, so the setup can take up to 40 seconds before the CGW fetch and compose even start, while the Maestro step waiting for e2e-draft-setup-ready gives up after 30 seconds (draftNetworkTimeout in apps/mobile/e2e/utils/scripts/defaults.js:6, gated in apps/mobile/e2e/tests/transactions/draft-editors/approval-editor.yml:19-22). On a slow staging network the flow can fail while the setup is still in progress and would otherwise have succeeded, making the suite flaky; the setup's wait attempts should be reduced or the gate timeout raised so the two align, with a comment explaining the relationship between the numbers.

The timeout error path in waitFor (the 'timed out waiting for …' error and the resulting 'failed' status) is never exercised because the test mocks selectChainById and getSafeSDK to succeed on the first try, leaving that failure branch untested.

The spender address is defined twice, once as SPENDER_ADDRESS and again as hand-written hex embedded inside APPROVE_DATA, creating two copies of the same value that could drift out of sync; building the calldata with Interface.encodeFunctionData('approve', [SPENDER_ADDRESS, amount]) would keep a single source of truth.

The too-low nonce test branch hardcodes 99999 and depends on the live staging Safe's current nonce staying below that value, silently coupling the test to on-chain state that could eventually change as the test Safe ages.

The nonce assertion on the transaction details screen checks that the copied nonce text appears anywhere on screen rather than being tied to the specific Nonce row, so it could match unrelated fields like SafeTxGas, BaseGas, or GasPrice that are often 0.

The spender text assertion regex '.*0x81Bd.*4fec.*' only matches 8 hex characters total, so any short-form address that happens to start with 0x81Bd and end with 4fec would also pass; a stronger assertion would match the full shortened form the UI actually renders.

The setup-status marker only signals ready or failed and never resets to idle between runs; resetReduxForE2E and the current call ordering in setupApprovalDraft happen to make this correct today, but if that ordering changes the marker could remain stuck at ready from a prior run.
If the fixture Safe's owners change, the hardcoded addresses will no longer match the fixture, and the setup will silently build a signer and spender that are out of sync with no warning.

After switching back to the recommended nonce, a small nonce value could coincidentally match one of the other zero-valued fields on the details screen, allowing the test to pass even if the Nonce row itself were incorrect.

The same 7-line block that scrolls to the edit-approval-button and taps it is duplicated at two locations in the file, despite the PR already extracting other repeated steps into utils/components/draft-editors/, where this block could also be moved.

Setting accessible={false} on the outer overlay Pressable removes the tap-outside-to-dismiss action from VoiceOver/TalkBack, so screen-reader users must rely on the Cancel button instead; this tradeoff is currently framed in the PR body as a pure accessibility improvement rather than being called out explicitly.

E2E_OWNER_ADDRESS and SPENDER_ADDRESS are hardcoded literals that duplicate mockedActiveSafeInfo.owners[0] and owners[1] from mock data, instead of being derived from the shared mock data as a neighboring setup file does.

The waitFor helper uses `if (value)` to check readiness, which rejects falsy-but-valid values like 0, '', or false; this works today only because both readers return objects, and is a footgun for future callers of this generic helper unless changed to a `value != null` check.

The unit tests only cover the setup timeout/failed marker for the case where composeSafeTxDraft rejects, but do not cover the waitFor timeout path that throws after POLL_ATTEMPTS when chain config or the Safe SDK never arrives, which is a more likely CI failure mode.
The review-and-confirm-button element is added in its own commit but no flow in this diff actually uses it, leaving unused code that should either be wired into a flow or deferred to a later PR.

setupApprovalDraft mixes dispatch sources, using the passed-in Dispatch for setupSendFlow but store.dispatch for the RTKQ and compose calls; since this is E2E-only code and store is already imported, using store.dispatch consistently throughout would be simpler.

The setupSendFlow test does not assert that router.replace('/(tabs)') was called, leaving a coverage gap for navigation behavior that is core to the setup's job since Maestro flows depend on landing on the home tab.

resetReduxForE2E is mocked to do nothing in this test file, so the real Redux store's signer, active-signer, and active-Safe state carries over between tests instead of being reset in beforeEach, unlike the sibling walletConnectDappsSetup.test.ts which resets the real slice; nothing fails currently only because all three tests happen to write the same values, but a future test expecting a clean store would behave differently depending on test order.
The unit test repeats the owner address literal again instead of importing the shared constant, compounding the duplication.
